issues.description: Silent behavior change: coerceNumber maps null/undefined to 0 instead of NaN like the old toNumber pipeline.
issues.detail: The old panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber directly; non-numeric domain entries propagated as NaN. The new coerceNumber returns 0 on null, which silently produces a bogus finite domain instead of NaN. That is a runtime semantic change smuggled in under a 'just adding types' PR. Either keep toNumber's return shape or document and test the new behavior.

issues.description: Three patches submitted as one: type annotations, a new runtime error, and a semantics-changing identity/coerce rewrite.
issues.detail: The commit message claims 'same runtime behavior as before, I just added types,' but the diff also throws on empty domains and swaps toNumber/identity-from-accessors for local reimplementations. These are three reviewable changes. Split into: pure type annotations, the empty-domain guard with its tests, and the helper substitution with justification. Bisecting a regression here will hit a commit doing all three.

issues.description: Gratuitous local identity reimplementation when accessors.identity already exists and was used previously.
issues.detail: The old code imported identity from './accessors.js'. The new file drops that import and inlines `const identity: TransformFn = x => x`. If the existing identity has the wrong type, fix its type at the source; don't fork a second identity in this module. Bad taste: adds a parallel name for an existing concept.

issues.description: isNonEmpty type guard buys nothing because domain[0] and peek(domain) are still indexed unconditionally afterward.
issues.detail: After `if (!isNonEmpty(domain)) error(...)`, TypeScript still sees `domain: number[]` in the rest of the body unless `error` is declared as `never`-returning. If it is, the guard is fine but the NonEmptyArray type never gets used downstream. Either lean on the peek overload added in this same PR or drop the helper; right now it's ceremony.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new error path covers Linear only; Log/Pow/Symlog variants are untested.
issues.detail: Only panLinear and zoomLinear get empty-domain tests. The guard lives in the shared pan/zoom helpers so the others get it transitively, but if anyone later inlines or refactors them the regression won't be caught. Two more one-line `t.throws` cases cost nothing and lock the contract.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the empty-domain check, defeating part of the new guard.
issues.detail: `panLog` and `zoomLog` call `Math.sign(domain[0])` in the wrapper before delegating to `pan`/`zoom`, which is where the empty-domain error lives. On `[]` they compute Math.sign(undefined) = NaN, then enter pan/zoom and throw. Functionally OK, but the guard's location is inconsistent with where the precondition is actually first violated. Move the check to the public entry points or document the order.

review.summary: The PR is sold as type-only but ships two real behavior changes: an empty-domain throw and a coerceNumber that maps null to 0 where the old code would have produced NaN. That second one is a silent semantic shift hiding inside a refactor PR and is the thing most likely to bite later. The peek overload and Domain/Anchor types are fine. NEEDS-WORK: split the patch, restore or explicitly document the null-handling change, drop the duplicate local identity, and add Log/Pow/Symlog empty-domain tests.
